subject: CatalystAI: follow-up — model fit checklist & prompt set request
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@catalyst.ai>, Priya Menon <priya@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — model fit checklist & prompt set request

Hi Amit / Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on your search-and-summarization pilot and the high-risk edge cases (legal clauses, redacted PII, and multi-document chains). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can start a short eval: 

- Goal: validate model quality on your 3 lanes (search-first extract, multi-doc summarization, and compliance redaction).
- Redwood asks: sample prompts + representative edge cases (CSV preferred, see attached template).
- Recommended models to try (fast iteration): Falcon-40B-Instruct, Mistral-Instruct-7B, and Llama-2-13B-chat quantized. We will run the same set across these variants and share token-latency tradeoffs.

Action items:
1) Could you upload 20–30 representative prompts and 10 redaction edge cases to the shared Drive folder by EOD Wednesday? (example rows: user_query, doc_snippet, expected_behavior)
2) Share any internal redaction rules (PII definition, retention policy) or attach a redaction sample PDF.
3) If you have benchmark expectations (e.g., ROUGE/EM or human quality thresholds), paste them into the Drive doc or reply here.

Attachments: catalyst_prompt_samples_v1.csv (template)

I'll loop in Marissa to propose the initial evaluation plan once we have your samples.

Thanks,

Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri_yom@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference for production
From: Amit Shah <amit@catalyst.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@catalyst.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — model fit checklist & prompt set request

Priyom — thanks for the summary. We're aligned and appreciate the concrete ask. A couple of clarifications: 

- For redaction, our definition of PII includes: names, SSNs, email addresses, phone numbers, and account numbers. We also need to flag legal identifiers in contracts (clause ids).
- For multi-doc summarization, edge case: linked footnotes that should be preserved as references (we'll mark those in the sample).

We've attached an initial CSV with 12 prompts and 6 edge cases. You'll see some rows intentionally include 'masked' PII and some raw examples we can't share — we'll paste the masked versions. Expect the drive upload for the full set tomorrow.

Attachment: catalyst_prompt_samples_v1.csv (12 example rows)

Two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood will perform automated redaction checks or only quality scoring?
2) Is the eval environment representative of hosted latency (i.e., same GPU configuration), or a best-effort CPU simulation?

Best,
Amit
VP Product, CatalystAI
amit@catalyst.ai | +1 212-555-0199

Thanks Amit — good questions. Short answers: 

1) Redaction checks: we will run an automated PII-detection pass as part of the eval (to surface failures), and a manual verification on a sampled subset for quality gating. We'll share a redaction-failure report that flags false negatives/positives.
2) Eval environment: we'll run evaluations on dedicated GPU instances that mirror hosted performance (same runtime config as Redwood Dedicated). We'll capture token latency and cost per response so you get apples-to-apples comparisons.

Plan: once we have your full prompt set, Marissa will propose an evaluation matrix (models x prompt variants x metrics) and a short timeline (typically 3–5 business days for the first sweep).

If you can upload the full CSV to the Drive link by end of day tomorrow, we'll queue the run. I've attached the template again for easy reference.

Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood eval plan + recommended model variants and benchmarks

Hi Amit / Priya — adding the evaluation details and quick model recommendations so you have something concrete to review.

Evaluation matrix (initial sweep):
- Models: Falcon-40B-Instruct, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Llama-2-13B-chat-quant (q4_0).
- Prompt variants: user-level, system-prompted safety wrapper, and redaction-first pre-processing.
- Metrics: task-specific exact/ROUGE where applicable, redaction false negative rate, human preference (blind A/B on 200 samples), latency p95, and cost/token.
- Timeline: 3 business days after sample upload for first pass; two additional days for manual QA and a short follow-up report.

Benchmarks and links:
- Internal benchmark results (same models on similar retrieval workloads): https://redwood-internal.company/benchmarks/catalystai-2026
- Eval run template (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_exampleCatalyst

Attachments: redwood_eval_recs_20261018.pdf (detailed plan)

A couple of notes:
- If CatalystAI requires deterministic behavior for legal extractions, we'll include a token-filtering pass and an extraction confidence threshold.
- For redaction-sensitive prompts, please mark which rows must never contain PII in the output (we'll treat those as hard constraints).

I'll build the initial job once the CSV is in the folder.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
